cohort: 409 Chinese women with a previous history of cesarean delivery and a singleton gestation in the vertex position, who underwent a trial of labor after cesarean (TOLAC)
finding: Shorter mid-trimester cervical length (MCL) was associated with a greater chance of VBAC, independent of other factors in the updated Grobman's predictive model.
mod_finding: While a shorter mid-trimester cervical length was associated with a higher chance of successful vaginal birth after cesarean, adding this factor to the Grobman's predictive model did not significantly improve its accuracy in predicting VBAC success.
